claim: As of 2026 shadcn/ui's manual install tells users to `pnpm add shadcn` as a project dependency and to put `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css";` in globals.css alongside `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));` — so shadcn is no longer a zero-CSS, zero-dependency copy-paste kit.
quote: pnpm add shadcn class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react tw-animate-css ... @import "tailwindcss"; @import "tw-animate-css"; @import "shadcn/tailwind.css"; @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));

claim: shadcn's May 2026 changelog states `init` now adds `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"` to global CSS, that the file holds shared Tailwind utilities/custom variants, and that `shadcn eject` inlines it and removes the dependency.
quote: inlines `shadcn/tailwind.css` into your global CSS file and removes the `shadcn` dependency from your project ... shared Tailwind utilities that both libraries depend on, e.g. custom variants like `data-open:` and `data-closed:` and utilities like `no-scrollbar` ... a small dependency that is tree-shaken in production and resolved at build time

claim: The npm package `shadcn` (v4.13.0, 'Add components to your apps.') genuinely exports a CSS file: its exports map contains "./tailwind.css": "./dist/tailwind.css", alongside ./registry, ./mcp, ./utils, ./icons and ./preset entrypoints.
quote: "./tailwind.css": "./dist/tailwind.css"

claim: The shipped shadcn/dist/tailwind.css is ~16 KB and contains accordion @keyframes, ~9 @custom-variant data-* variants (data-open/data-closed/data-checked/data-unchecked/data-selected/data-disabled/data-active/data-horizontal/data-vertical), a no-scrollbar utility, and scroll-fade/shimmer utilities — but NO colour tokens, NO :root/.dark blocks and NO `@custom-variant dark` definition; it only consumes `@variant dark` inside the shimmer utility.
quote: @custom-variant data-open { &:where([data-state="open"]), &:where([data-open]:not([data-open="false"])) { @slot; } } ... @utility no-scrollbar { -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none; ... } ... @variant dark { --_highlight: var(--shimmer-color, ...); }

claim: A 2026 community discussion titled 'Why does shadcn components suddenly depend on npm i shadcn' documents user backlash that Switch and other newer components stop working without `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"`, which requires the `shadcn` npm package — breaking the 'copy the code, own it' premise.
quote: It seems like an implementation done by someone who couldn't imagine the implications of it.

claim: The June 2026 chat-interface components release states the new scroll-fade and shimmer utilities ship inside shadcn/tailwind.css, confirming the CSS package is the shipping vehicle for new shadcn primitives.
quote: Both utilities ship with `shadcn/tailwind.css`, so projects initialized with `npx shadcn@latest init` already have them.

claim: The shadcn Vite installation page itself only tells the user to hand-write `@import "tailwindcss";` in src/index.css and install tailwindcss/@tailwindcss/vite/@types/node — the shadcn dependency and the shadcn/tailwind.css + @custom-variant dark lines are emitted by `npx shadcn@latest init`, not typed by the user.
quote: @import "tailwindcss";

claim: Tailwind v4 has no built-in class-based dark mode: you must declare a custom variant, either against a class or against a data attribute — this is the single hook every kit must be wired into.
quote: @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));  /* data attribute variant */  @custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *));

claim: MUI's colorSchemeSelector accepts 'class' (emits .light/.dark), 'data' (emits [data-light]/[data-dark]), or a custom %s selector such as '.theme-%s'; without it MUI dark mode is driven by prefers-color-scheme and cannot follow a .dark class toggle.
quote: createTheme({ colorSchemes: { light: true, dark: true }, cssVariables: { colorSchemeSelector: 'class' } });  // CSS Result  .light { ... }  .dark { ... }

claim: The MUI System CSS-theme-variables API types colorSchemeSelector as `'media' | 'class' | 'data' | string`; the docs page does not state which value is the default.
quote: colorSchemeSelector: 'media' | 'class' | 'data' | string

claim: MUI requires InitColorSchemeScript's `attribute` prop to match the theme's colorSchemeSelector; with attribute="class" it writes <html class="dark">, which is exactly the element Tailwind's .dark custom-variant keys off, so one toggle can drive both.
quote: When customizing the `attribute` prop, make sure to set the `colorSchemeSelector` in the theme to match the attribute you are using. ... <InitColorSchemeScript attribute="class" />

claim: MUI's official Tailwind v4 integration page covers only CSS cascade layers (@layer theme, base, mui, components, utilities + enableCssLayer) and contains NO dark-mode/colour-scheme guidance — the dark-mode wiring is left to the separate CSS-theme-variables docs.
quote: @layer theme, base, mui, components, utilities; @import 'tailwindcss';

claim: MUI issue #41511 ('Is there any way to apply the Tailwind's `dark:` class prefix?') documents that Tailwind dark: utilities like 'bg-slate-300 dark:bg-slate-800' do not work on MUI components out of the box in a default MUI dark-mode setup.
quote: Is there any way to apply the Tailwind's `dark:` class prefix? ... bg-slate-300 dark:bg-slate-800 ... that doesn't work.

claim: MUI issue #38575 reports the docs-site dark mode toggle not updating [data-mui-color-scheme] and thereby mis-styling the Tailwind demos — a concrete instance of MUI and Tailwind dark state drifting out of sync.
quote: [website] Dark mode toggle doesn't affect [data-mui-color-scheme]

claim: MantineProvider sets data-mantine-color-scheme on <html>; every Mantine component style keys off that attribute, and useMantineColorScheme/useComputedColorScheme are the toggle API. The attribute name is not documented as configurable (only the colorSchemeManager storage is).
quote: the `data-mantine-color-scheme` attribute is used in all component styles to determine which colors each component should use

claim: The documented community recipe for one toggle driving both Mantine and Tailwind v4 is to redefine Tailwind's dark variant against Mantine's attribute rather than a .dark class, so both read the same DOM attribute and hydration cannot mismatch.
quote: @custom-variant dark (&:where([data-mantine-color-scheme=dark], [data-mantine-color-scheme=dark] *));

claim: Mantine's own discussion on using Tailwind together with Mantine warns that Tailwind's base/preflight styles conflict with Mantine components — the colour-scheme sync problem sits on top of an existing reset conflict.
quote: you can use Mantine with Tailwind CSS without additional setup ... make sure not to include Tailwind base styles as they will conflict with some Mantine components

claim: Base UI ships no CSS, no theme and no colour-scheme system at all: setup is just the package plus optional `isolation: isolate` on the root; dark mode is entirely the consumer's Tailwind @custom-variant, so there is nothing to keep in sync.
quote: since Base UI is unstyled, you can use CSS-in-JS, plain CSS, or any other styling solution you prefer

claim: shadcn maintainers/community confirm `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));` in globals.css is not a shadcn invention but plain Tailwind v4 manual-dark-mode syntax; it is the single line that makes both Tailwind's dark: utilities and shadcn's .dark token block respond to the same .dark class.
quote: It's a native feature of TailwindCSS for handling dark mode

claim: shadcn's Tailwind v4 page shows the token model — light values on :root, overrides in a .dark block, re-exported to Tailwind via @theme inline — and instructs replacing the @plugin 'tailwindcss-animate' with @import "tw-animate-css".
quote: :root { --background: hsl(0 0% 100%); --foreground: hsl(0 0% 3.9%); } .dark { --background: hsl(0 0% 3.9%); --foreground: hsl(0 0% 98%); } @theme inline { --color-background: var(--background); --color-foreground: var(--foreground); }
